workload.description: 150k rps peak through a gateway that consults a shared token-bucket tier before every upstream call; 7% of requests are throttled

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: c6g.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); arm64 (Graviton2). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.068/h x 730 = 4964c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.r7g.large — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.t4g.medium — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.065/h Single-AZ x 730 = 4745c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 150,000 req/s peak at the edge. 92.9% pass the limiter and reach the upstream, 7% are throttled and returned a 429 without ever touching it, 0.1% are policy refreshes pulling rule changes.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Redis holds the AUTHORITATIVE counters and is consulted on every single request — it carries the full 150k rps and is the design's binding shared state. Two nodes at ~100k ops/s each is the whole safety margin; lose one and the tier is at 150% instantly. That fragility is the lesson of this design.

assumptions.subject: throttling
assumptions.statement: Throttling is modelled as a SHORTER PATH, not as dropped load: the 7% still costs the limiter and Redis a full round trip, and only the upstream is spared. That is why rejecting traffic does not make a rate limiter free.

assumptions.subject: consistency
assumptions.statement: A distributed token bucket needs atomic increments and clock agreement. The engine models the Redis round trip's THROUGHPUT and LATENCY only — it has no notion of atomicity, of a slightly-over-limit race across shards, or of local-cache-then-sync approximations. Treat the counts as a capacity result, never as a correctness proof.

assumptions.subject: db
assumptions.statement: The policy store is nearly idle by design — limit rules are read once and cached. It is in the model because it still costs money and still fails; it is not there to carry load.

_library.summary: Gateway-fronted distributed rate limiter with shared Redis token buckets, where rejected traffic still costs a full counter round trip.
